source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: MusicBrainz full export 20261024-102842 (musicbrainz_fullexport_LATEST: '20261024-102842'; mbdump.tar.bz2, sha256 in musicbrainz_fullexport_20261024_SHA256SUMS), schema sequence 31 (Default.pm: 'sub ACTIVE_SCHEMA_SEQUENCE { 31 }'; DDL pinned to musicbrainz-server commit bade3a567e20ec69323ac7850fca9d0ee113f87d): the unpack step extracts the PostgreSQL COPY files mbdump/<table> for the ten tables and writes musicbrainz/<table>.tsv (tab-separated, \N for NULL converted to empty, UTF-8) with the column names of CreateTables.sql in DDL order as header; root release_country left-joined to release on release = release.id, release_group on release.release_group, release_group_primary_type on release_group.type, artist_credit on release.artist_credit, release_status on release.status, release_packaging on release.packaging, language on release.language, script on release.script, and area on release_country.country = area.id (country references country_area.area, a subset of area.id); shared column names are prefixed by their table (release_gid, release_group_gid, release_artist_credit, release_group_artist_credit, release_group_type, *_name); dropped: release.name and release_group.name (free text), release.barcode, release.comment, release_group.comment, quality, edits_pending, last_updated, artist_credit.ref_count, created and gid, the parent, child_order, description and gid columns of the lookup tables, language.iso_code_1, iso_code_2b, iso_code_2t and frequency, script.iso_number and frequency, and all area columns but name; release_country has several million rows, which the loader samples to 1,000,000.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table release_country: "ALTER TABLE release_country ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_pkey PRIMARY KEY (release, country);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table release_country: "release INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- PK, references release.id", "country INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- PK, references country_area.area"
truth.justification: (release, country) is the declared composite primary key of release_country, the root table, and the three date parts are its other columns.

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release_country ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_pkey PRIMARY KEY (release, country);" + "release INTEGER NOT NULL, -- PK, references release.id country INTEGER NOT NULL, -- PK, references country_area.area"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table release_country: "ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_fk_release FOREIGN KEY (release) REFERENCES release(id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table release: "ALTER TABLE release ADD CONSTRAINT release_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"
truth.justification: release is a foreign key to the declared primary key of release, so it determines the columns of the one release row (gid, artist_credit, release_group, status, packaging, language, script).

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release_country ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_fk_release FOREIGN KEY (release) REFERENCES release(id);" + "ALTER TABLE release ADD CONSTRAINT release_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateIndexes.sql, table release: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX release_idx_gid ON release (gid);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table release: "gid                 UUID NOT NULL,"
truth.justification: gid is NOT NULL and covered by a unique index, so it is an alternate key of release and determines id, hence every release column.

audit.quote: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX release_idx_gid ON release (gid);" + "id SERIAL, gid UUID NOT NULL, name VARCHAR NOT NULL, artist_credit INTEGER NOT NULL, -- references artist_credit.id release_group INTEGER NOT NULL, -- references release_group.id"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table release: "ADD CONSTRAINT release_fk_release_group FOREIGN KEY (release_group) REFERENCES release_group(id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table release_group: "ALTER TABLE release_group ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"
truth.justification: release.release_group is a foreign key to the declared primary key of release_group, so it determines the columns of the one release-group row (gid, artist_credit, type).

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release ADD CONSTRAINT release_fk_release_group FOREIGN KEY (release_group) REFERENCES release_group(id);" + "ALTER TABLE release_group ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateIndexes.sql, table release_group: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX release_group_idx_gid ON release_group (gid);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table release_group: "gid                 UUID NOT NULL,"
truth.justification: gid is NOT NULL and covered by a unique index, so it is an alternate key of release_group and determines its id.

audit.quote: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX release_group_idx_gid ON release_group (gid);" + "gid UUID NOT NULL, name VARCHAR NOT NULL, artist_credit INTEGER NOT NULL, -- references artist_credit.id type INTEGER, -- references release_group_primary_type.id"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table release_group: "ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_fk_type FOREIGN KEY (type) REFERENCES release_group_primary_type(id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table release_group_primary_type: "ALTER TABLE release_group_primary_type ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_primary_type_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table release_group_primary_type: "name                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,"
truth.justification: release_group.type is a (nullable) foreign key to the declared primary key of release_group_primary_type, whose row carries the name (third step of the chain (release, country) -> release -> release_group -> type -> name); a null type keeps '?' on both sides.

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release_group ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_fk_type FOREIGN KEY (type) REFERENCES release_group_primary_type(id);" + "ALTER TABLE release_group_primary_type ADD CONSTRAINT release_group_primary_type_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table release: "ADD CONSTRAINT release_fk_artist_credit FOREIGN KEY (artist_credit) REFERENCES artist_credit(id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table artist_credit: "ALTER TABLE artist_credit ADD CONSTRAINT artist_credit_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table artist_credit: "name                VARCHAR NOT NULL,", "artist_count        SMALLINT NOT NULL,"
truth.justification: release.artist_credit is a foreign key to the declared primary key of artist_credit, whose row carries the credit name and the artist count; release_group.artist_credit is a separate foreign key to the same table and the DDL does not require the two to be equal, so release_group_artist_credit determines nothing here.

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release ADD CONSTRAINT release_fk_artist_credit FOREIGN KEY (artist_credit) REFERENCES artist_credit(id);" + "ALTER TABLE artist_credit ADD CONSTRAINT artist_credit_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);" + "name VARCHAR NOT NULL, artist_count SMALLINT NOT NULL,"

truth.justification: release.language is a (nullable) foreign key to the declared primary key of language, whose row carries the name and the ISO 639-3 code.

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateIndexes.sql, table language: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX language_idx_iso_code_3 ON language (iso_code_3);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateTables.sql, table language: "iso_code_3          CHAR(3)  -- ISO 639-3"
truth.justification: iso_code_3 is covered by a unique index but is nullable (no NOT NULL in CreateTables.sql), so it is unique only among non-null values: several languages without an ISO 639-3 code share the empty value and determine different ids; unsure for that reason.

audit.quote: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX language_idx_iso_code_3 ON language (iso_code_3);" + "iso_code_3 CHAR(3) -- ISO 639-3"

truth.justification: release.script is a (nullable) foreign key to the declared primary key of script, whose row carries the name and the ISO 15924 code.

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release ADD CONSTRAINT release_fk_script FOREIGN KEY (script) REFERENCES script(id);" + "ALTER TABLE script ADD CONSTRAINT script_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"

truth.justification: iso_code is NOT NULL and covered by a unique index, so it is an alternate key of script and determines its id (and, through it, script_name); rows whose release has no script keep '?' on both sides.

audit.quote: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX script_idx_iso_code ON script (iso_code);" + "iso_code CHAR(4) NOT NULL, -- ISO 15924"

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table release_country: "ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_fk_country FOREIGN KEY (country) REFERENCES country_area(area);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table country_area: "ALTER TABLE country_area ADD CONSTRAINT country_area_pkey PRIMARY KEY (area);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreateFKConstraints.sql, table country_area: "ADD CONSTRAINT country_area_fk_area FOREIGN KEY (area) REFERENCES area(id);"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/musicbrainz_CreatePrimaryKeys.sql, table area: "ALTER TABLE area ADD CONSTRAINT area_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);"
truth.justification: country references the primary key of country_area, which is itself a foreign key to the declared primary key of area, so country identifies one area row and determines its name; the join goes to area directly on id.

audit.quote: "ALTER TABLE release_country ADD CONSTRAINT release_country_fk_country FOREIGN KEY (country) REFERENCES country_area(area);" + "ALTER TABLE country_area ADD CONSTRAINT country_area_pkey PRIMARY KEY (area);" + "ALTER TABLE country_area ADD CONSTRAINT country_area_fk_area FOREIGN KEY (area) REFERENCES area(id);" + "ALTER TABLE area ADD CONSTRAINT area_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);" + "Areas that can be used for filling in the Release country field of releases are listed, by ID, in the country_area table."
